name: Air Fryer Teriyaki Beef Meatball Bowls
method: Mix the meatball ingredients and roll into 16 meatballs (4 servings).
Spray with olive oil and air fry at 200°C (400°F) for 15-18 minutes.
Make the cucumber salad: toss the sliced cucumbers with chilli crisp, rice vinegar, soy sauce, green onions and sesame seeds.
Assemble each bowl with 1 cup cooked jasmine rice, a serving of meatballs, cucumber salad, 1/2 cup shredded iceberg lettuce, 1 cup steamed broccoli and 1/4 cup steamed edamame.
Top with 1 tbsp teriyaki sauce, green onions and sesame seeds.
author: Natalie Fardone

name: Baked Pipe Rigate with Spicy Vodka Sauce
method: Melt butter in a large pot.
Add sliced onions and sauté in melted butter.
Stir in garlic and tomato paste.
Sprinkle in chili flakes for heat.
Pour in vodka and let it cook off for a minute.
Add cream and stir into the sauce until it's a vibrant orange color.
Mix the cooked pipe rigate pasta into the sauce.
Tip the pasta into a baking dish and top with freshly grated parmesan.
Bake in a hot oven (about 220°C) for 8-10 minutes until golden.
Finish with a drizzle of olive oil before serving.
notes: The original has no quantities; amounts are a guide for 4.
author: Broadsheet Melbourne

name: Beef and Vegetable Rice Bowl
method: In a bowl, marinate beef, sliced onions with soy sauce, vinegar, salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, gochujang, minced garlic, and chili flakes.
Marinate for at least 30 minutes (or overnight).
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sautée beef until browned and fully cooked.
Assemble your bowls with jasmine rice, beef, kimchi, cucumber, shredded carrots, and edamame.
notes: Marinate the beef for at least 30 minutes, or overnight.
author: Sweet Eats by J

name: Beef Wellington with Chestnut Stuffing & Roasted Cranberries
method: For the mushroom stuffing: Add chestnuts, shallots, celery, and garlic to a food processor and pulse until finely chopped. Transfer to a large bowl. Add mushrooms to the food processor and pulse until mushrooms are pea-sized. Transfer to the bowl along with salt and pepper; stir to combine.

Melt beef tallow in a large heavy skillet, preferably cast iron, over medium-high heat. Add mushroom mixture, thyme, and bay leaves and stir to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally, until most of the liquid has evaporated and mushrooms are beginning to brown, 10 to 12 minutes. Season, remove bay leaves, and set aside to cool. Chill for at least 1 hour and up to 24 hours.

For bone broth reduction: Heat beef tallow in a large skillet over medium high and add shallots, garlic, thyme, bay leaves, and peppercorns and cook, tossing occasionally until just beginning to brown, about 4 minutes.

Remove from heat and carefully add bourbon, return to heat and tilt skillet toward flame to ignite. Cook until flames have died and almost all of the liquid has evaporated. Add bone broth and cook, stirring occasionally, until reduced by half, about 45 minutes. Strain, discard solids, and keep warm until ready to serve.
For the beef: Season the tenderloin with salt and pepper. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and chill for at least 1 hour and up to 24.

Once beef is chilled, heat beef tallow in a large skillet over high until very hot. Cook tenderloin, turning every 30 to 60 seconds, until all sides and the ends are browned, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a platter and brush all sides with Dijon mustard. Let rest for 30 minutes.

On a clean work surface, overlap long sheets of plastic wrap. Place crepes on top to make about a 14- by 7-inch rectangle, overlapping slightly so they are large enough to cover the tenderloin. Shingle bresaola over the crepes. Spread the chilled mushroom mixture over the bresaola in an even layer. Sprinkle apricots over top.

Place the beef along one long end and roll tightly around the tenderloin using the plastic to help you, peeling it back as you roll. Wrap the whole thing tightly in the plastic, twisting both ends like a candy wrapper. Chill for at least 30 minutes and up to overnight.

Heat oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a rimmed baking sheet with baking paper. Whisk the egg with 1 teaspoon water. Roll out about 450g of the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface to a 15- by 14-inch rectangle and lay it on baking paper. Brush egg over a rectangle about as wide as your piece of meat, leaving a 1-inch border.

Unwrap the beef log and place it along one long side of the pastry. Roll up tightly, then place seam-side down on the baking sheet. Tuck the pastry over the ends, pinching to seal and folding underneath. If adding a lattice, freeze for 10 to 15 minutes.

Lattice (optional): brush the pastry with egg, roll a lattice cutter across the remaining puff pastry and lay it over the top and sides. Press to adhere, brush with egg, and top with flaky salt and pepper. Freeze for another 10 to 15 minutes.

Bake until the pastry is golden brown all over and the meat is cooked to your liking (it will climb about 5°C while resting), about 40 to 50 minutes. If the pastry is already golden after 30 minutes, tent with foil. Rest on a wire rack for 20 minutes, leaving the oven on.

For the roasted cranberries: toss the cranberries with the sugar, wine, olive oil, rosemary, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Spread on a lined tray and bake at 220°C until bubbling, 20 to 30 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes.
Slice the Wellington into thick pieces. Serve with the broth reduction and roasted cranberries.
notes: A make-ahead project: the stuffing, broth reduction and wrapped beef can all be done the day before.
author: Rick Martinez

name: Bocconcini Stuffed Meatballs
method: Preheat oven to 200c.
Combine all meatball ingredients except bocconcini in a bowl.
Divide mixture into 12 portions. Flatten each portion, place a bocconcini ball in the centre and seal the meat around it forming a meatball.
Place into an oiled baking dish and bake for 20 minutes until golden and brown.
While the meatballs are cooking, heat oil in a pan on medium heat and cook onions for 5 minutes until softened. Add garlic and cook for a further minute.
Stir in tomatoes, oregano, salt + pepper and simmer for 10 minutes. Serve and enjoy.
author: Mary Hoffmann

name: Breaded Fish with Sauce Vierge
method: To make the sauce vierge, put the coriander seeds into a small pan and toast for 2 minutes until fragrant. Pour in the olive oil and add the lemon zest and tomatoes and heat gently until the tomatoes are just soft. Add the lemon juice and capers, season lightly and remove from the heat.
Put the seasoned flour, egg and breadcrumbs into 3 separate, shallow bowls, then toss the fish fillets first in the flour, then the egg and finally the breadcrumbs.

Heat 1cm of oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Carefully lower in the fillets and fry for 2-3 minutes on each side until really golden, then drain on kitchen paper and season with sea salt flakes.
Stir the herbs through the sauce vierge and serve with the fish and buttered new potatoes, if you like.
notes: Plaice is hard to find in Australia: flathead or whiting fillets work well.
author: Adam Bush

name: Chicken & Brothy Rice
method: Mix the marinade together in a bowl. Add half to the chicken and mix to coat.
Air-fry at 180C for 20 mins, flipping halfway (or pan fry for 5-7 mins each side) until cooked through then slice.
Cook the rice per packet instructions.
Add remaining marinade to a saucepan with the chicken bone broth. Mix well and bring to the boil.
Add the Asian vegetables and simmer for a few minutes until softened.
Divide the cooked rice, greens, broth and chicken between 2 bowls. Garnish with green onion, chilli oil and sesame seeds to serve.
author: Miranda Brady

name: Chicken Curry Laksa
method: Soak the dried chillies in hot water for 10 minutes, then blend with the ginger, peeled garlic, fresh chillies, shallots, lemongrass, oil, shrimp paste and spices to a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in the oil over medium heat, stirring, for 5-8 minutes until fragrant and darkened. Add the thick cream from the top of one can of coconut milk and fry for a few minutes more.
Add the remaining coconut milk, stock, sugar and chicken thighs. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until the chicken is cooked; remove and shred or slice it. Add the tofu puffs and season with salt.
Cook the noodles according to the packet and divide between bowls.
Ladle the soup over the noodles, top with the chicken, halved eggs, cucumber, bean sprouts and mint, and serve with lime wedges and sambal oelek.
notes: The original method wasn't saved; these steps are a guide. A good jar of laksa paste works as a shortcut for the homemade paste.
author: Andy Baraghani

name: Chicken Filo Pie
method: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the sliced leek and sauté for 4 minutes, then add the carrots and sauté for a further 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, and thyme for another 2-3 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir continuously for 1–2 minutes.

Gradually pour in the chicken stock while stirring to avoid lumps. Add the pecorino, black pepper, salt, frozen peas, and shredded roast chicken. Mix well and allow everything to heat through for 3-4 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to an ovenproof dish. Layer scrunched filo pastry sheets on top, brushing with melted butter to create a golden, crispy finish.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 20 minutes or until the filo pastry is golden and crisp.
Let it cool slightly before serving. Enjoy!
author: @keetasdishdiaries

name: Chicken Katsu Smashed Tacos
method: Mix together ingredients for chicken filling until well combined.
Spread an even, thin layer on each tortilla, leaving a 1cm border around edges.
Brush with egg then sprinkle with panko breadcrumbs, dusting off excess.
Generously drizzle oil into frypan and place over medium heat.
Once hot, place taco, chicken-side down into pan. Cook for 3-4 mins or until golden and flip. Cook for another 2-3 mins.
For the slaw, place all ingredients in a bowl and toss well.
Assemble tacos by topping with slaw, spring onion, tonkatsu sauce and sesame seeds.
author: Sophie Fisher

name: Chicken Meatballs with Orzo
method: Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Mince the garlic and chop up the shallot. Slice up one lemon.
In a bowl mix the ground chicken with the breadcrumbs, feta cheese and parsley. Season with salt and pepper, mix well and shape into medium-sized meatballs.
Heat up a splash of olive oil in a cast iron skillet and cook the meatballs until browned on all sides (keep the heat on medium and watch them as they cook fast and can burn easily).

Remove the meatballs to a plate and cook the garlic and shallot for 30 sec until fragrant. Add the lemon slices and cook for another 30 sec. Add the orzo, season with salt and pepper and toast for a minute or two. Add the heavy cream, chicken broth and spinach and mix until the spinach is wilted.
Nestle the meatballs in the skillet and bake for 20–25 minutes until the liquids are absorbed and the orzo is fully cooked.
author: Vanya Hajnas

name: Chicken Ruby
method: For the marinade, blitz the ingredients together in a blender to a smooth paste. Transfer to a bowl.
Cut the chicken into 4cm chunks. Add to the marinade and turn to coat. Cover and leave to marinate in the fridge for 6–24 hours.
Heat the grill to medium-high. Place the marinated chicken on a rack in the grill pan, brush with the melted butter and grill for 8–10 minutes, until cooked through and nicely charred.
Warm a large saucepan over a medium-low heat. Add the makhani sauce, cream and grilled chicken and simmer very gently for 10 minutes.
Serve the curry garnished with ginger matchsticks, chopped coriander and pomegranate seeds, with a bowl of steamed rice on the side.
notes: Dishoom-style butter chicken. Needs one quantity of makhani sauce (not included here). Marinate the chicken 6-24 hours.
author: R Dozo

name: Chicken Stir-Fry
method: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a saute pan over medium heat. Add garlic and stir. Place the chicken in the pan and brown 4 minutes on each side. Remove from pan, slice into strips, set aside.

Heat remaining tablespoon of oil in a wok over high heat. Add the vegetables and teriyaki sauce. Stir-fry quickly until the vegetables begin to soften. Add the chicken strips, combine well and continue to cook for 2 to 3 minutes. Serve immediately.
author: Tyler Florence

name: Chicken Teriyaki
method: Simmer the soy sauce, sugars, garlic, ginger, pepper, cinnamon stick and pineapple juice with 1/2 cup water until the sugar dissolves. Cool.
Pour half the sauce over the chicken thighs and marinate in the fridge for at least an hour, ideally overnight.
Grill or pan-fry the chicken over medium-high heat until charred and cooked through, about 5 minutes a side. Rest, then slice.
Bring the remaining sauce to a simmer, stir in the cornflour mixed with a little water, and cook until glossy and thick.
Serve the chicken over rice with the sauce spooned over.
notes: Marinate the chicken for at least an hour, ideally overnight. The original method is behind the NYT paywall; these steps are a guide.
author: John T. Edge

name: Chicken Tikka Wraps
method: Mix all chicken tikka ingredients in a bowl. Add chicken, coat well, and marinate for at least 30 mins (or up to 4 hrs).
Air fry at 180°C for 15 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Mix all sauce ingredients in a bowl until smooth. Chill until ready to use.
Warm each wrap in a dry pan for 30–60 seconds per side.
Spread yogurt sauce on each wrap, add chicken and greens, fold, and serve.
notes: Marinate the chicken for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).
author: Isabella Raso

name: Chili Crisp Beef Bowls with Coconut Broth
method: Cook rice according to package directions, adjusting portion sizes as needed.

Meanwhile, heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Drizzle with oil, then add the ground beef, breaking it into small pieces as it browns. Once the beef is almost fully cooked, add the pepper, onion and garlic and sauté until softened.

Mix together the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, chili crisp, ginger powder and broth then add to the beef mixture, stirring to combine. Reduce the heat and allow the sauce to slightly cook down. If needed, season with salt.
For the broth, add coconut milk, soy sauce, chili crisp and ginger to a sauce pan. Bring to a boil and stir to combine all ingredients.
Assemble bowls by adding rice, then topping with beef, broth, cucumbers.
author: Ellen Speaker | Forget the Takeout

name: Chilli Cheese Loaded Mash
method: Boil the potatoes until tender, then mash with the butter, a splash of milk, salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, soften the diced onion in the olive oil, then brown the beef mince.
Stir in the chilli powder, paprika, garlic powder and tomato purée for a minute, then add the chopped tomatoes, drained kidney beans and beef stock. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Spoon the mash into bowls, top with the chilli and the mozzarella and cheddar, and grill or air fry briefly to melt the cheese.
notes: The original has no method; these steps are a guide.
author: Kirsty Fletcher

name: Chopped Chicken Salad
method: Make the dressing: whisk the soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, sesame oil, avocado oil, lemon juice and sugar.
Add the chopped iceberg, wombok and green beans to a large bowl.
Add chopped spring onions and coriander to the bowl.
Add the shredded roast chicken to the bowl.
Pour dressing over the ingredients in the bowl and toss with tongs.
Sprinkle sesame seeds over the mixed salad.
author: Jem Lester

name: Coconut Chilli Ramen with Crispy Pork
method: Add minced garlic, ginger, and lemongrass to a pan with oil and heat.
Stir in peanut butter, red curry paste, miso paste, and chicken broth.
Pour in coconut milk, soy sauce, and lime juice, then add crispy chilli oil to taste.
In a separate hot pan, add small clumps of pork and cook until crispy.
Season pork with hoisin, black bean, and soy sauce.
Prepare a bowl with cooked noodles, ladle in soup, top with crispy pork, diced cucumbers, and a soft-boiled egg.
Garnish with green onions, sesame seeds, and a lime wedge before serving.
notes: The original has no quantities; amounts are a guide for 4.
author: The Good Bite

name: Creamy Butter Bean & Roasted Veg Agnolotti
method: Roast the chopped veg with olive oil and seasoning at 200°C until soft.
Blend with the drained butter beans, then add the passata and blend until creamy.
Cook the agnolotti, toss through the sauce and finish with Parmesan.
author: Eisha-Marie Eisel

name: Crispy Chicken Caesar Sandwiches
method: Preheat oven and toast prepared bread rolls with herb butter and parmesan cheese.
Mix mayonnaise with minced garlic, minced anchovies, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and black pepper to make the Caesar dressing.
Toss shredded cos lettuce with the Caesar dressing to coat evenly.
Cook chicken schnitzels until golden brown and crispy.
Assemble the sandwich by placing a chicken schnitzel on toasted garlic bread, topping with Caesar salad and more grated parmesan.
Place the top half of the toasted garlic bread onto the sandwich and serve.
author: Nicole Maguire

name: Easy Beef Pie
method: Preheat your oven.
Chop the onion and celery. Grate the carrot, zucchini, and garlic.
Heat olive oil in a wide, deep pan. Add onion, carrot, zucchini, celery, and garlic. Sprinkle salt and cook until soft.
Add fresh thyme, oregano, and tomato paste. Stir well.
Add flour and mix to thicken.
Pour in red wine vinegar, beef stock, and Worcestershire sauce.
Add ground beef, salt, and black pepper. Cook until beef is browned and mixture thickens.
Peel and slice potatoes very thinly. Use a mandoline for even slices if possible.
Layer the potato slices over the beef mixture in a concentric circle.
Drizzle melted butter over the potatoes.
Cover the pan with aluminum foil and place in the oven to bake until the potatoes are golden and crispy.
Garnish with fresh thyme leaves before serving.
notes: The original has no quantities; amounts are a guide for 4.
author: Nicole Maguire

name: Easy Beef Taco Bowls
method: Make a quick salsa: mix the tomato, red onion, finely chopped jalapeño, coriander, 2 tbsp lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Blitz the brown onion, garlic and coarsely chopped jalapeño to a paste (or chop very finely).
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high, add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned and crisp in places.
Add the onion paste and cook until the liquid evaporates, then stir in the taco seasoning with a splash of water and the remaining lime juice.
Serve over rice with the salsa, avocado, lettuce, corn chips and lime wedges.
notes: The original method wasn't saved; these steps are a guide.
author: Rachel Gurjar

name: Fish en Papillote (Fish in a Bag)
method: Preheat oven to 190°C / 375°F (170°C fan-forced).

Cook potato - Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes and cook for 4 minutes, stirring regularly (use 2 wooden spoons if needed). They should pick up a little colour but not too much.
Cook the rest of vegetables - Add the zucchini, capsicum, red onion, garlic and half of the salt and pepper. Toss everything together for about 1 minute, then set aside.

Place two pieces of foil on your work surface (50cm / 20" long x 30cm / 12" wide), then top with a sheet of baking paper/parchment paper (40cm / 16" x 30cm / 12"). Divide the vegetables between the two, placing them in the middle. (Note 4)
Fish - Pat the snapper fillets dry, season both side with the remaining salt and pepper, then place on top of the vegetables.
Place 3 dill sprigs on top of each fish. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil and pour 1 tbsp of white wine over each.

Build the parcels (video is helpful here) - Bring the short edges of the foil and baking paper together and fold over twice to seal that side. Press down gently along the fold to flatten it. Then, working on one end, fold each corner in to form a triangle, then fold that triangle over twice more to lock in the seal. Repeat on the other end so both ends are sealed the same way. Redo the same with the other parcel.
Bake & rest - Place the parcels on a baking tray and cook for 18 minutes. Remove and let rest for 3 minutes. (Once cooked, the core fish temperature should read at least 55°C / 130°F.)
Serving - Grand opening time! Open the parcels, watch the steam escape, squeeze some lemon juice over and eat while hot with some crusty bread on the side.
author: Chef JB (RecipeTin)

name: Gochujang Coconut & Lime Brothy Rice
method: Put rice on to cook and marinate your chicken, leave for at least 15 minutes to marinate whilst you cook rice.
In a separate pan, make your broth. In a pan on medium heat with neutral oil, add garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant. Then add gochujang. Cook for a few minutes until it deepens.
Stir through bone broth and coconut milk, soy sauce, rice wine vinegar. Leave to simmer gently whilst you cook your chicken.
Sear chicken in pan or cook in air fryer at 180°C for 10 minutes until cooked through.
Squeeze lime juice through broth before serving.
Plate your rice, pour over broth and top with chicken and choice of veggies.
author: Siân Ruffell

name: Hailey Bieber Chicken Meatballs
method: Combine all MEATBALL ingredients into a bowl. Roll into 16 small balls.
Heat 1/2 tbsp olive oil in a pan and sear/cook the meatballs. Add another 1/2 tbsp olive oil before turning them over. Set aside.
Pour 1 tbsp olive oil into the same pan, add diced brown onion, and cook until soft and caramelised. Just before it's fully done, stir in minced garlic and cook until aromatic.
Pour in the passata, add 2 tsp sugar and salt, and let it simmer for about 5 minutes.
Return the meatballs to the pan and heat through before serving.
Top with cottage cheese (~40g), parmesan (~10g), and fresh basil.
author: Julz Yap

name: Hainanese-Inspired Chicken Rice and Broth
method: Start with the broth, add all the ingredients to a pot, simmer with the lid on.

For the rice, sauté the ginger and spring onion in the neutral oil for 1-2 min before adding in the washed rice & sesame oil. Give a mix then add in the chicken stock. Cook using the absorption method until it's nice and fluffy.
For the chicken, mix together all the ingredients except the chicken breast. Coat the chicken in the marinade.

Fry both sides of the chicken in neutral oil until charred on medium heat. Add in the leftover sauce once chicken is cooked. Cook for a further 1 min. Remove from the pan & cook the bok choy plus the remaining chicken stock in it.
For the chilli lime sauce, heat the neutral oil and carefully pour over the garlic and chilli. Add in the sesame oil, soy sauce & lime juice. Mix.
Assemble. Place rice on the bottom, pour in the broth, chicken & bok choy on top, garnish with spring onions & cucumber. Spoon over the chilli lime sauce.
author: Lucy Rosenberg

name: High Protein McChicken Smash Tacos
method: In a small bowl, mix together the light mayo and Miracle Whip until smooth. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, mix ground chicken with garlic powder, black pepper, and salt.
Press a thin layer of seasoned chicken onto the back of each flour tortilla, making sure it covers the surface evenly. Then sprinkle on the breadcrumbs for that added crunch factor.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a little avocado oil. Place the tortilla chicken-side down and cook for 3-4 minutes until the chicken is golden and fully cooked. Flip and crisp up the tortilla side for another 2-3 minutes.
Spread a generous amount of McChicken sauce over the crispy chicken, top with shredded lettuce, and fold it up like a taco.
author: Torin Redpath

name: Hot Honey Crispy Chicken Bowls
method: Rice: Cook rice in a rice cooker or any preferred way.
Cucumber salad: Mix the cucumber with some salt and let it sit for 5-10 mins, rinse then mix with the rest of the ingredients and set aside.
Mix the tenderloins with soy, rice wine, baking soda and seasonings, mix well until no liquid remains and the chicken has absorbed it.
Add the cornstarch and mix until all the chicken is evenly coated, spray with some oil spray and airfry at 200c for 12-14 mins, shaking halfway.

To a hot pan on medium/hot heat, add sesame oil, garlic and chilli and sautee. Add the honey, allulose, soy, sriracha and rice wine vinegar and let it slightly bubble and cook for a minute, add the chicken stock cornstarch slurry, lower the heat and mix until thickened. Add the cooked chicken and some sesame seeds and mix until well coated.
Plate up with cooked rice, crispy chicken, cucumber salad, edamame and purple cabbage. Top with green onion & sesame seeds.
author: Eliya Hachem

name: Jamie's Courgette Carbonara
method: Put a large pan of salted water on to boil.

Halve and then quarter any larger courgettes lengthways. Cut out and discard any fluffy middle bits, and slice the courgettes at an angle into pieces roughly the same size and shape as the penne. Smaller courgettes can simply be sliced finely.
Add the penne to the boiling water and cook according to the packet instructions.
Separate the eggs and put the yolks into a bowl. Add the cream and grate in half the Parmesan, and mix together with a fork. Season lightly with salt and pepper, and set aside.
Heat a very large frying pan and add a good splash of olive oil. Cut the bacon into chunky lardons and fry until dark brown and crisp.

Add the courgette slices and 2 big pinches of black pepper. Pick, chop and sprinkle in the thyme leaves, stir so the courgettes are coated in the bacon-flavoured oil, and fry until lightly golden and slightly softened.

Work quickly now: drain the pasta, reserving a little of the cooking water. Immediately toss the pasta in the pan with the courgettes and bacon, then remove from the heat and add a ladleful of the cooking water and the creamy sauce. Stir together quickly (no more cooking, or the eggs will scramble).
Grate in the rest of the Parmesan and add a little more cooking water if needed for a silky, shiny sauce. Taste for seasoning and serve immediately.
author: Jamie Oliver

name: Marry Me Chicken
method: Halve the chicken breasts horizontally into cutlets, season with salt and pepper, and dust with flour.
Brown the chicken in olive oil and a little of the butter over medium-high heat, 3-4 minutes a side. Set aside.
Lower the heat, add the remaining butter, garlic, tomato paste, oregano and chilli flakes and cook for a minute.
Add the stock, scraping up the browned bits, then the cream, parmesan and sun-dried tomatoes. Simmer until slightly thickened.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan and simmer for a few minutes until cooked through. Scatter with basil to serve.
notes: The original method is behind the NYT paywall; these steps are a guide. Good with crusty bread, pasta, rice or a green salad.
author: Naz Deravian

name: Massaman Curry (Chicken)
method: Toast the cardamom, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, cinnamon and cloves in a dry pan until fragrant, then grind with the nutmeg and mix into the red curry paste.
Spoon the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into a pot and fry over medium heat until it starts to split. Add the curry paste and fry for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the shallots and chicken and stir to coat, then add the rest of the coconut milk, the potatoes and peanuts. Simmer gently for 20-25 minutes until the chicken and potatoes are tender.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and tamarind, tasting and adjusting until salty, sweet and sour are balanced.
Serve with jasmine rice, topped with coriander and extra peanuts.
notes: The original method is behind the NYT paywall; these steps are a guide. Don't shake the coconut milk: the thick cream on top is used to fry the paste. Swap the chicken for beef, prawns or tofu if you like.
author: Naz Deravian

name: Miso Peanut Ramen Bowls
method: Press tofu with paper towels to remove some of the water. Grate tofu on a box grater, on medium / large holes.
Heat olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tofu shreds and salt; saute until golden and lightly crisped, 10-15 minutes.
Add the teriyaki sauce and grated garlic to the tofu. Sauté for another 5-10 minutes to caramelize further. Transfer to a separate bowl and wipe out the pan.

In the same pan, heat the curry paste, miso, peanut butter, soy sauce, and brown sugar until it's worked into a thick paste. Add the coconut milk and broth, and whisk until incorporated. Simmer for 5-10 minutes.
Add ramen (just the noodles, not sauce packets) directly into the simmering broth. They will cook in 4-5 minutes; let it simmer for 1-2 minutes longer to thicken.
Serve ramen in bowls, with a scoop of broth over the top. Top with the tofu, herbs, and chili crisp.
author: Lindsay Ostrom

name: Mushroom Risotto with Peas
method: Bring the stock to a simmer in a saucepan and keep it warm. Season with salt.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the shallots until tender, then add the mushrooms and cook until they release their liquid and it evaporates. Add the garlic and thyme and season.
Add the rice and stir until the grains are coated and crackling, then add the wine and stir until absorbed.
Add the stock a ladleful at a time, stirring often and adding more each time it's nearly absorbed, for about 20-25 minutes, until the rice is creamy and just tender.
Stir in the peas, another ladle of stock, the parsley and parmesan. Season and serve straight away.
notes: Use vegetable stock to keep it vegetarian. The original method is behind the NYT paywall; these steps are a guide.
author: Martha Rose Shulman

name: One-Pan Italian Sausage Tuscan Pasta
method: Cook the pasta in salted water, reserving some pasta water.
Remove casing from sausage links and cut into small pieces.
Brown sausage pieces in a pan with olive oil over medium heat.
Add diced shallots and minced garlic to the pan; stir and cook until soft.
Add tomato paste, sun-dried tomatoes, Calabrian chili, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and Italian seasoning to the pan and mix well.
Add pasta water and heavy cream, stirring to combine the sauce evenly.
Stir in freshly grated Parmesan and let the sauce simmer.
Add baby spinach and cooked pasta to the sauce, tossing to coat.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
Add torn pieces of burrata, if using, before serving.
author: Cup of Liv

name: Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccoli Rabe
method: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering. Pinch the sausage into small pieces into the pan in a single layer. Cook, undisturbed, until the bottom is light golden brown, about 2 minutes, then turn the pieces. Add garlic, anchovy (if using), and pepper flakes, and cook until fragrant, 30 seconds to 1 minute.

Increase heat to medium-high and add wine. Bring to a simmer and cook, swirling and scraping up any stuck-on bits, until the wine has emulsified with the oil and reduced slightly, about 30 seconds. Turn off heat.

Add the broccoli rabe stalks (with florets) to the boiling water and cook until barely tender, 1 1/2 to 2 minutes. Scoop out onto a plate. Add the leaves and cook about 1 minute, then scoop out, keeping the water boiling. Cut stalks and florets into 1 1/2-inch pieces and combine with the leaves.

Add orecchiette to the boiling water, stirring for the first 30 seconds. After 5 minutes, transfer 1 cup of pasta water to the skillet along with the broccoli rabe. Bring the skillet to a boil over high heat, swirling until the water emulsifies with the oil, 1 to 2 minutes.
Cook the pasta until about 3 minutes short of the packet time, then transfer it to the skillet (reserve at least 2 cups pasta water).
Cook on high, stirring and tossing, until the pasta is al dente and the sauce coats it, 2 to 3 minutes, adding more pasta water a little at a time. Keep it slightly looser than you want to serve it.
Remove from heat, stir in 3/4 of the cheese, and season with salt. Serve immediately with the remaining cheese.
notes: Broccoli rabe is sold as rapini or cime di rapa; broccolini works as a swap.
author: Sasha Marx

name: Oven-Baked Doner Kebab
method: Place the beef in a bowl. Grate in the onion, press in the garlic, and add a few spoons of Greek yoghurt and the spices.
Mix well by hand, then spread the mixture onto baking paper and roll into a tight log.
Put the log on a baking tray with sliced red onions and tomato wedges and bake at 200°C for about 35-40 minutes until cooked through.
Slice the meat thinly and serve in pita bread with the onions, tomatoes, pickled peppers and white garlic sauce (or yoghurt mixed with garlic).
notes: The original has no quantities; amounts are a guide for 4.
author: Yumna | Feel Good Foodie

name: Panko Chicken Schnitzel with Brown Butter & Capers
method: Set the flour, eggs, and panko in three separate shallow bowls. Season the chicken cutlets with salt and pepper. Dredge the chicken in the flour, shaking off any excess, then dip in the eggs and coat thoroughly with the panko, pressing lightly to adhere.

In each of 2 large skillets, heat 1/4 cup of canola oil. Add the chicken and cook over moderately high heat, turning once, until golden and crispy, about 3 minutes per side. Transfer the chicken to a paper towel-lined baking sheet and sprinkle with salt, then transfer to plate.

Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, melt the butter and cook over moderately high heat until browned and nutty, about 4 minutes. Stir in the capers, lemon juice, and parsley; spoon over the chicken and serve.
author: Thomas Keller

name: Pasta alla Vodka
method: Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water until just shy of al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water and drain.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large pan and cook the pancetta (if using) until crisp. Add the onion, garlic and chilli flakes and cook until soft.
Add the vodka and simmer until reduced by about half, then add the crushed tomatoes, season and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cream, then add the pasta and toss with the parmesan and a splash of pasta water until glossy.
Finish with oregano and parsley and serve with extra cheese.
notes: The pancetta is optional; leave it out for a vegetarian version. The original method is behind the NYT paywall; these steps are a guide.
author: Colu Henry

name: Pasta alla Zozzona
method: Cook rigatoni per the packet directions.
In a small bowl, beat the egg yolks and Pecorino cheese together with a fork until a thick paste forms. Season with a few grindings of black pepper and stir in 1/4 cup of pasta water. Set aside.
Drizzle the oil into a large pan. Add the sausage and use a wooden spoon to break it into pieces as it cooks.
Add the guanciale to the pan. Once it turns golden and crispy, add the onion and garlic.
When the onion becomes translucent, add the passata. Stir gently and cook on medium-low heat for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle fresh basil into the sauce and stir gently. Then, add the cooked pasta together with the egg yolk and Pecorino cheese mixture.
Stir and toss until the pasta is well coated. Finish by adding more Pecorino cheese and black pepper.
author: On Trac 5

name: Pasta with Pumpkin Brown Butter Sauce
method: In a large, deep skillet of simmering salted water, cook the pasta until al dente. Drain, reserving 1 cup of pasta cooking water.

In a small skillet over medium-high heat, melt the butter. Add the crushed red pepper flakes, minced shallots, sage leaves, salt, and pepper. Whisk until butter begins to bubble and brown. Stir in the pumpkin butter, a splash of pasta water and whisk to combine until saucy. Toss with cooked pasta. Garnish with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.
author: Kelsey Jane Youngman

name: Peanutty Chicken Salad
method: Butterfly the raw chicken breast and pop it in the air fryer for 10 mins before shredding (pan-frying would work too).
Prep the salad bits and make the dressing in the meantime.
Toss everything together and top with the peanuts and sesame seeds.
author: Emma Petersen

name: Peking-Style Beef
method: Pour cooking oil into a hot skillet. Add the beef and break it up with a spatula. Cook until it starts caramelising on the edges.
Mix hoisin sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar and a pinch of Chinese five-spice in a bowl.
Add the garlic to the beef and stir, then pour over the sauce and mix until the meat is coated.
Stir in a cornflour slurry and keep stirring until glossy.
Serve over white rice with cucumber ribbons, garnished with spring onions, a drizzle of sesame oil and sesame seeds.
notes: The original has no quantities; amounts are a guide for 4.
author: Nicole Maguire

name: Pork and Spring Onion Dumplings with Crispy Skirt
method: Finely chop the spring onions and grate the ginger. Mix with the pork, 2 tsp soy sauce, 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper.
Place a heaped teaspoon of filling on each wrapper, wet the edge and fold into a half-moon, pleating to seal.
Whisk 1 cup water with 2 tbsp rice vinegar, the flour, cornflour and a pinch of salt to make the slurry.

Heat a little oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high. Arrange the dumplings flat-side down, pour in enough slurry to come a few millimetres up the sides, cover and cook until the water evaporates and a lacy golden crust forms, about 8 minutes.
Invert onto a plate, crust side up. Mix the remaining soy sauce and vinegar (and chilli oil) for dipping.
notes: Makes 24. The original method wasn't saved; these steps are a guide.
author: Sohla El-Waylly

name: Pork Mince Stir Fry with Cabbage Slaw
method: Finely shred the cabbage and toss with half the sesame oil, the rice vinegar and a pinch of sugar. Set aside to lightly pickle.
Grate the ginger and garlic and slice the spring onions, keeping the whites and greens separate.
Heat the remaining sesame oil in a wok over high heat. Add the pork mince and fry, breaking it up, until browned and a little crispy.
Add the ginger, garlic and spring onion whites and cook for a minute. Stir the miso and soy into the water and add to the pan, cooking until saucy.
Serve the pork over rice with the cabbage slaw, sesame seeds and spring onion greens.
notes: The original method wasn't saved; these steps are a guide.
author: Adam Bush

name: Prawn Stir Fry
method: Steam broccolini: Steam broccolini until crisp-tender, about 2 - 3 minutes (remember it will cook more in the stir fry). Set aside to drain and dry.
Stir Fry Sauce: Put all Stir Fry Sauce ingredients except water into a bowl. Mix until cornflour is dissolved. Then stir in water.

Cook then remove prawns: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet on medium to medium-high heat. Add prawns and spread them in a single layer. Cook for 1 1/2 minutes, then turn and cook the other side for 1 minute until cooked through. Try not to make the prawns too golden (they are only lightly browned in stir fries). Remove prawns to a bowl. Set aside.

Cook onion, garlic and ginger: Add more oil if the pan seems a bit dry. Still on medium-high heat, add onion and cook for 1 minute. Then add ginger and garlic and cook for another 1 minute until onion is starting to soften but not colour.
Add snow peas, then broccolini: Add snow peas and toss until coated with oil. Then add broccolini and toss through.

Add Sauce and thicken: Give the Sauce a stir (to dissolve cornflour settled at bottom), then pour into skillet. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens to syrup consistency (about 1 minute) and coats the ingredients nicely.
Add prawns back in: Then add the prawns back in (including any juices in the bowl). Toss for another 30 seconds until prawns are warmed through.
Serve: Serve with rice!
author: Nagi

name: Restaurant-Quality Beef Massaman Curry
method: Cut the beef into large chunks and sear in the olive oil until browned all over. Set aside.
Cook the curry paste with half a can of coconut cream for 5-10 minutes, until the oil separates and rises to the top.
Add the beef, onions, potatoes, carrots, the rest of the coconut cream and the water. Season with palm sugar, fish sauce and tamarind.
Slow cook for about 4 hours, or until everything is fork tender and the meat falls apart. Taste and adjust the salty, sour and sweet to your liking.
Serve with rice, topped with herbs and chopped salted peanuts.
notes: Uses Maesri massaman curry paste (yellow can). Slow cook for about 4 hours until the beef falls apart.
author: Jasmin's Eats

name: Ribeye Steak
method: Pat the steaks dry and season generously with salt and pepper. Leave at room temperature for 30 minutes if you can.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the steaks and cook, flipping every minute or so, until well browned, 8-10 minutes for medium-rare (52°C inside).
Turn the heat to low, add the butter, shallot and herbs, and baste the steaks with the foaming butter for a minute or two.
Rest the steaks for 5-10 minutes, then slice and spoon over the pan butter.
notes: The original method is behind the NYT paywall; these steps are a guide. Good with a rocket salad, green beans or potatoes.
author: Ali Slagle

name: Sausage and Pea Orzo Risotto
method: Heat the oil in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it up into small pieces until no longer pink.
Add the shallot and sauté until translucent, about 1 minute. Add the orzo and water or stock, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.

Bring to a boil, then cover, and reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the orzo has absorbed all the liquid and is cooked through (add more liquid if the orzo starts to dry out or stick). Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Stir in the peas, and allow to cook for a minute or two just to thaw. Remove from the heat, and stir in the Parmesan and parsley. Serve immediately.
author: Kerry Saretsky

name: Slow Cooker Creamy Pesto Chicken
method: Add your chicken, diced onion, garlic puree, chicken stock, pesto and sundried tomatoes to the slowcooker and cook on high for 3-4 hours or low for 7-8.
Once ready, add your frozen peas and some creme fraiche. Give that a good stir then prepare your orzo. If the sauce is runny add cornflour.
Cook your orzo as per packet instructions then serve immediately, topped with parmesan.
author: Bored of Lunch

name: Slow-Roasted Crispy Pork Belly
method: Dry skin overnight: Place pork belly on a plate. Pat skin dry with paper towels. Leave uncovered in fridge overnight to dry out the skin. (If you don't have time, pat the skin dry as best you can).
Preheat oven to 140°C/285°F (120°C fan).
Season flesh: Drizzle flesh (only) with 1 tsp oil. Sprinkle over 1/2 tsp salt, the pepper and fennel powder. Rub all over the flesh, including on the sides.

Wrap in foil: Place 2 pieces of foil on a work surface. Put the belly in middle of foil, skin side up. Fold the sides in to enclose the belly, forming an open box, pinching corners to seal tightly and make it as snug as possible. Place meat on a tray.
Season skin: Pat skin dry with paper towels. Rub with 1/2 tsp oil then sprinkle remaining 1/2 tsp salt evenly all over the skin surface.
Slow roast 2 1/2 hours: Roast for 2 1/2 hours. After 1 1/2 hours, remove and tighten the foil (pork will have shrunk), and continue cooking.
Increase heat: Remove pork from oven, then increase heat to 240°C/465°F (all oven types).
Level pork: Remove pork from foil and place on a rack set over a tray. Use scrunched up balls of foil under the pork so the skin is as level as possible.
30 minutes on high heat: Roast for 30 minutes, rotating after 15 minutes as needed, until the crackling is deep golden, puffy and crispy all over. Protect any patches browning too fast with foil.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice into 2cm thick slices with a serrated knife. Serve with apple sauce.
notes: Dry the skin in the fridge overnight if you can. Don't score the skin.
author: Nagi

name: Smash Burger Tacos
method: Press 50 grams of beef mince into each corn tortilla.
Season with taco seasoning.
Place tortillas face down on a pan and cook until crispy.
Flip and add cheese, allowing it to melt.
For the sauce, mix Greek yogurt with sriracha, taco seasoning, and tomato sauce.
Top cooked tortillas with sauce, lettuce, tomato, onion, and pickles.
notes: Amounts are per person: scale up for the household.
author: Madeleine Storace

name: Soy Crumbed Chicken with Garlic Rice & Veggies
method: Make garlic rice: finely chop or crush garlic. In a medium saucepan, melt the butter with a dash of olive oil over medium heat. Cook 1/2 the garlic until fragrant, 1-2 mins. Add jasmine rice, the water and a generous pinch of salt and bring to the boil. Reduce heat to low and cover. Cook for 10 mins, then remove from heat and keep covered until rice is tender and water absorbed, 10 mins.

Cook veggies: slice carrot into thin sticks and trim green beans. In a large frying pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over high heat. Cook carrot and green beans until slightly softened, 4-5 mins. Add remaining garlic and 1/2 the soy sauce and cook until fragrant, 30 seconds. Transfer to a plate and cover to keep warm.
Combine the BBQ sauce, sweet chilli sauce and vinegar in a small bowl.

Cook chicken: pound chicken between baking paper until about 1cm thick. Set up three bowls: flour with salt and pepper; egg whisked with the remaining soy sauce; panko breadcrumbs. Dip chicken into flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat enough olive oil to coat the base of the frying pan over medium-high heat and fry chicken until cooked through, 3-4 mins each side. Drain on paper towel.
Slice chicken. Divide garlic rice and veggies between bowls, top with the chicken and spoon the BBQ sauce mixture over to serve.
notes: From a meal-kit card, so it has no quantities; amounts are a guide for 2.
author: R Dozo

name: Spaghetti Carbonara
method: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil.
Whisk the eggs, yolks, pecorino, parmesan and plenty of coarse black pepper in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the guanciale until the fat renders and the edges are crisp. Turn off the heat.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente, reserving a cup of pasta water. Add the pasta to the guanciale pan and toss to coat.
Off the heat, pour in the egg mixture and toss quickly, adding splashes of pasta water until the sauce is creamy and glossy, not scrambled. Serve with extra pecorino and pepper.
notes: The original method is behind the NYT paywall; these steps are a guide. The goal is creaminess: keep the heat off when the eggs go in.
author: Ian Fisher

name: Spicy Coconut Beef Broth Bowls
method: Add all of the broth ingredients to a pot and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

While the broth simmers, heat a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic until softened and fragrant, about 2-3 minutes. Add the ground beef and cook until mostly browned. Stir in the ginger, soy sauce, and sriracha, then cook for another 2-3 minutes until fully cooked through.
To serve, add jasmine rice and the beef mixture to a bowl. Ladle over the warm broth and top with sliced cucumbers and a drizzle of chili oil.
author: Kelsey

name: Steak au Poivre & Frites
method: Frites: cut the potatoes into thin chips, dry them extremely well and toss with plenty of olive oil and sea salt flakes. Spread on a lined tray, not touching, and bake at 200°C for about 30 minutes until super golden and crispy.
Season the steak with lots of sea salt flakes and freshly ground pepper.

Place half the butter in a pan over high heat, and when it begins to foam, sear the fillets on each side to gain a crust and cook 3/4 of the way through. Remove from the pan and rest. Don't clean the pan out.
Add the rest of the butter and the cracked peppercorns and fry off.
Deglaze with the Cognac, and flambé the contents of the pan if you're confident, or reduce by half.
Pour the cream into the pan and allow to bubble lightly, add the steak back in and finish cooking gently.
Pour the sauce over the steak and serve with hot frites.
author: Laura Sharrad

name: Thai Chicken Cashew
method: Make the Sauce: Mix all the sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
Cook Aromatic: Heat vegetable oil over high heat in a wok or large pan. Add garlic and onion, stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add Chicken: Add the sliced chicken. Cook for about 1–2 minutes until the outside changes from pink to white.
Add Vegetables: Stir in the white parts of the spring onions, red capsicum, cashews, and the sliced chili. Stir fry until the chicken is cooked, around 2 minutes.
Add Sauce: Pour in the sauce. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until it reduces to a syrupy consistency and coats the chicken.
Finish with Spring Onions: Add the green parts of the spring onions. Toss for 30 seconds.
Serve: Transfer to a serving dish. Serve with jasmine rice and garnish with extra spring onion and red chilli if desired.
author: @keetasdishdiaries

name: Thai Green Curry
method: Heat oil in a heavy based skillet or pot over medium high heat.
Add curry paste (and garlic, ginger and lemongrass extras, if using a jar paste) and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until it mostly "dries out".
Add chicken broth and coconut milk, mix to dissolve paste. Season with 1 tsp fish sauce and 1 tsp sugar for jar paste (3 tsp of each plus 1/8 tsp salt for homemade paste).
Add kaffir lime leaves. Mix then bring to simmer.
Add chicken, stir then lower heat to medium so it's bubbling gently. Cook 7 minutes.
Add eggplants, cook 5 minutes until soft.
Taste sauce. Add fish sauce or salt for more saltiness, sugar for sweetness.
Add snow peas, cook 2 minutes until a bit softened, then stir through basil and lime juice. The sauce should still be on the thin side; don't keep simmering or it will darken.
Serve curry over jasmine rice with garnishes of choice.
author: Nagi

name: Thai Red Curry with Chicken
method: Heat oil in a large heavy based skillet over medium high heat.
Add curry paste and Extras (if using jar paste) and cook for about 2 minutes so it "dries out".
Add chicken broth and stir to dissolve paste. Simmer rapidly for 3 minutes or until liquid reduces by half.
Add coconut milk, lime leaves, sugar and fish sauce. Stir, then add chicken.
Spread chicken out, bring to simmer, then turn heat down to medium. Simmer for about 8- 10 minutes or until Sauce reduces, the chicken is cooked and the sauce is almost at the thickness you want.
Do a taste test. Add more fish sauce (or even shrimp paste) to add more saltiness, sugar for sweetness.
Add pumpkin and beans, stir. Cook for 3 minutes or until pumpkin is just cooked through and Sauce is thickened.
Remove from heat. Stir through a handful of Thai basil leaves.
Serve over jasmine rice, garnished with fresh red chilli slices and fresh coriander/cilantro leaves, if desired.
author: Nagi

name: Tomahawk Steak (Reverse Sear)
method: De-chill - Take the steak out of the fridge 1 hour prior to cooking. Remove from packaging and pat the surface dry. (Do not salt).
Preheat the oven to 140°C/285°F (120°C fan-forced).
Season - Sprinkle the steak meat with salt and pepper, then use your hands to rub it in.
Slow(ish) roast - Put the steak on a rack and set it on a baking tray. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, or until the internal temperature is 50°C/122°F (for medium rare).
Rest - Take the tray out of the oven and leave the steak on the counter for 10 minutes.
Preheat the BBQ on high until it's screaming hot.
Oil - Drizzle the oil on the steak and lightly pat to spread (don't rub off the salt).
Turn the BBQ down to low or medium-low just before putting the tomahawk on.
Edges first - Using tongs, hold the steak upright and sear the edges and bone first, rotating every minute or so. Watch for flare-ups.
Steak crust - Then place the steak down and cook for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, or until the internal temperature is 55°C / 131°F.
Rest the steak on a rack for 3 minutes - the internal temperature will rise to 57°C/135°F, which is perfect medium rare.
Serve - Cut into 1 cm / 0.4" thick slices and serve with steak sauce of choice.
notes: Use a meat thermometer. Serve with cowboy butter, béarnaise, mushroom sauce or chimichurri.
author: Nagi Maehashi

name: Turkey Burgers
method: Grate half the onion and mix gently with the turkey, Worcestershire sauce, ketchup, salt and pepper. Shape into 4 patties.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan or on a grill over medium-high and cook the patties for about 5 minutes a side until cooked through.
Toast the buns and build the burgers with sliced tomato, onion, lettuce, pickles, red capsicum, ketchup and mustard.
notes: The original method is behind the NYT paywall; these steps are a guide.
author: Martha Rose Shulman

name: Tuscan Chicken
method: Season the chicken with salt, pepper and half the Italian seasoning. Brown skin-side down in olive oil over medium-high heat until crisp, then flip and brown the other side. Set aside.
Soften the sliced onion in the same pan, then add the garlic, sun-dried tomatoes and remaining seasoning for a minute.
Add the white wine and let it bubble down by half, then add the stock and cream.
Return the chicken to the pan, skin-side up, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until cooked through.
Stir the spinach and parmesan into the sauce until wilted. Serve with mash or crusty bread.
notes: The original method wasn't saved; these steps are a guide. Serve with mash or crusty bread.
author: Adam Bush

name: Tuscan Chicken Orzo (Slow Cooker)
method: Add chicken, sun-dried tomatoes (with oil), garlic, broth, Italian seasoning, salt & pepper to the crockpot.
Cook on low for 4–5 hours, then shred the chicken.
Stir in orzo + milk. Cook 20–30 minutes until the orzo is tender.
Fold in spinach and parmesan until creamy and silky.
author: Valerie | Everyday Mom Finds

name: Vodka Orzo
method: Sauté shallot and garlic in olive oil and butter.
Add dried chili flakes and oregano.
Add tomato paste and let it caramelize.
Pour in vodka and cook for a few minutes.
Add orzo and stir.
Pour in chicken stock and cook for seven to ten minutes.
Add cream and Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper and mix.
Top with buffalo mozzarella, fresh basil, and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.
notes: The original has no quantities; amounts are a guide for 4. Uses chicken stock (swap for vegetable stock to keep it vegetarian).
author: What would Kayla cook?

name: Vodka Sauce Potato Bake
method: Preheat oven to 190°C fan-forced.
Make the sauce: heat the butter and olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the eschalots and sauté until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir in the tomato paste and cook until it deepens in colour and caramelises slightly.
Stir through the chilli flakes, then add the vodka. Cook for 1–2 minutes to allow the alcohol to cook off.
Pour in the cream and stir until smooth. Remove from the heat and stir through the parmesan until melted. Blend the sauce until smooth.
Stand the potato slices upright and tightly packed in a square baking dish. Pour the vodka sauce over the potatoes and top with sliced mozzarella.
Loosely cover with baking paper, then foil, and bake for 45 minutes. Uncover and bake for a further 20 minutes, until golden, bubbling, and the potatoes are tender.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
author: @keetasdishdiaries

name: Zucchini Carbonara
method: Heat oil and butter in a large, deep frypan over medium-high heat. Once butter melts and is foaming, add the zucchini and cook for 2-3 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked and golden. Use tongs to transfer to a plate and cover to keep warm. Add asparagus to same pan and cook, tossing occasionally, for 1 minute or until just tender, bright green and golden. Use tongs to transfer to plate with zucchini, cover to keep warm and set aside.

Add leek and garlic to the same pan and reduce heat to medium. Stir through spinach and cook, tossing occasionally, for 1 minute or until spinach wilts. Remove pan from heat and return zucchini and asparagus to pan.
At the same time, cook the spaghetti in a large saucepan of boiling, salted water according to packet directions (about 6-8 minutes) until al dente, reserving 3/4 cup (180ml) pasta water.

Meanwhile, whisk yolks, parmesan and 2 tbs cold water in a large jug. Season well. This is where you need everything ready to go, so that you can work quickly. Use tongs to transfer pasta from saucepan to frypan with the vegetables, and toss well to combine. Temper the egg yolk mixture with 1/2 cup (125ml) hot leftover pasta cooking water, whisking with a fork to combine, then pour over the pasta in frypan and toss quickly to coat and melt the cheese, and to work the starch in the pasta (this will help thicken the sauce).

If the carbonara looks a little dry, add more of the leftover pasta cooking water to loosen, up to another 1/4 cup (60ml). Toss through the lemon zest and juice and season well. Serve immediately, sprinkled with extra parmesan.
author: Tracey Pattison
